target_customer: Manufacturers with precision environments such as pharmaceutical, semiconductor and precision plants in Southeast Asia
problem: HVAC is a major energy cost in controlled-environment factories, and existing building management systems run it with static rules that waste energy.
business_model: B2B software and hardware control layer, likely subscription or savings-linked

founders.name: David Chew
education: First Class degree in Aeronautics (school not named)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder and calls him a former consultant.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs integration with BMS and IoT sensors plus control models that keep temperature, humidity and particle counts in spec. Physical integration and safety constraints are the hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Site-specific models and installed control integrations create some stickiness, but the approach was copyable by larger building AI vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found. The company reports continuing to operate at about 10 staff.

market_need_then: Industrial HVAC consumes large energy shares and manufacturers faced scope 2 emission pressure. The company claims up to 30 percent HVAC energy savings, a claim not independently verified.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, smarter greener more efficient facilities

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Axross is still active with about 10 staff and hiring in Kuala Lumpur and Penang. Public information is thin: no verified funding or customers were found, so its trajectory is unknown. It targets a real energy cost problem in regulated manufacturing, but without sourced traction no stronger conclusion is supportable.
